target_customer: At batch time ML engineers working with computer vision data; later operations leaders at quick service restaurants using security camera footage
problem: Computer vision teams struggled to validate and monitor models and data reliably, and later companies had oceans of video footage they could not turn into operational insight.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform (MLOps monitoring at first, later video intelligence for enterprises)
product_category: computer vision MLOps, later vision-language video intelligence

founders.name: Botty Dimanov
education: PhD in Explainable AI for Vision, University of Cambridge (YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists a US patent on extracting concepts from visual information and Forbes 30 Under 30 recognition.

founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in 2022 seed coverage (tech.eu via search summary); YC page lists only one founder.

founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in 2022 seed coverage (tech.eu via search summary); YC page lists only one founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision model diagnostics and later multimodal video understanding with emotion and gait analytics require advanced ML work; the CEO holds a Cambridge PhD in explainable vision AI.

defensibility.rationale: Computer vision tooling had several rivals, and the later video question answering product competes with large model providers; no structural moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; later large vision-language models from big labs expanded the field.

market_need_then: Seed coverage in 2022 described demand for more reliable computer vision software for ML engineers; later materials describe restaurants wanting insight from existing security cameras.

branding.community_and_virality: A 2022 business press piece used a Terminator themed headline about the company; no community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand specific coverage; trademark filings show the name is protected but nothing shows recognition.

pivots.why: Reason not found; date not found

outcome_analysis: Tenyks, a Cambridge spin-out, got 125 thousand dollars from YC and raised a 3.4 million dollar seed in March 2022 co-led by Speedinvest and firstminute capital. It later repositioned toward video intelligence and reports a Fortune 500 customer, but no later round or exit was found, so it stays small and active.
